title: Balanced Malaysian Tofu Curry
subtitle: with Quinoa and Spring Onion
description: Our 'balanced' recipes are just that – high in nutritive value (that's fibre-rich veggies, lean proteins and wholegrains, just between us), so these dishes are good for you in every which way! They're perfect for anyone looking to minimise their intake of refined foods without sacrificing on taste.

steps.text: Cook quinoa: Put the quinoa in a sieve, rinse well and drain (see Kitchen 101). Put in a small saucepan with 250ml (1 cup) water, cover and bring to a simmer. Reduce the heat to low and cook, covered, for 12-15 mins until the water is absorbed and the quinoa is tender. Turn off the heat and stand, covered, for 5 mins. Season with salt and pepper.

Prep ingredients: Meanwhile, crush or finely chop 1 garlic clove. Thinly slice the spring onion, keeping the white and green parts separate. Halve the carrot and zucchini lengthwise and thinly slice. Quarter the tofu pieces.
Start curry: Heat 2 tsp vegetable oil in a medium deep frypan over medium heat. Cook the curry powder, garlic and white part of the spring onion, stirring, for 1 min or until fragrant.

Simmer curry: Add the coconut milk, carrot, zucchini and 125ml (½ cup) water to the pan and bring to the boil, then reduce the heat to medium and cook for 3 mins. Add the tofu and cook for 2 mins or until the tofu is warmed through and the carrot is just tender.

Serve up: Stir ½ tsp soy sauce and ½ tsp white vinegar into the curry. Taste, then season with salt and pepper. Remove the pan from the heat. Divide the quinoa and tofu curry among bowls, scatter over the remaining spring onion and enjoy!
Kitchen 101: It’s important to rinse the quinoa well to remove the natural coating called saponin, which can make it taste bitter or soapy.
